perOption.label: (A)
perOption.reason: 'Just as today some jobs are better than others, so would they have been in early societies' — the correlative 'Just as ..., so ...' licenses subject-auxiliary inversion (so + aux + S), and 'would have been' is appropriate past conjecture about prehistoric societies. Attractive distractor: the inversion plus perfect modal looks exotic and tempts a flag, but 'so did/would + S' after 'just as' is a standard inversion pattern. Grammatical.

perOption.label: (B)
perOption.reason: Inside the absolute construction 'with some roles (being) more dangerous and some ___ more plentiful access', the second conjunct must parallel the first small clause with a non-finite predicate: 'some having more plentiful access'. A finite 'have' cannot head a with-absolute. Rescue readings fail: treating 'and some have ...' as a coordinated finite clause breaks the tense frame (past conjecture 'would have been' vs present 'have') and leaves 'with some roles more dangerous' dangling as a broken coordination. This is the error — governing rule: with + NP + participle (absolute construction) parallelism.

perOption.label: (C)
perOption.reason: 'Some individuals are buried with more precious goods' — passive voice (individuals are buried, not bury), descriptive/historical present consistent with the surrounding clauses ('some are in group graves'). Correct.

perOption.label: (D)
perOption.reason: 'still others don't even seem to be buried at all' — seem + to-infinitive passive; the referents undergo burial, so the passive infinitive is required and correctly formed. Correct.

perOption.label: (E)
perOption.reason: True subject is the plural head 'chemical and isotope analyses (of teeth and long bones)', so plural 'reveal' agrees. The usual proximity-attraction trap is defused because the nearest noun 'long bones' is also plural; either parse yields plural agreement. Correct.

Real-time pull check: (A) is the designed magnet — 'so would they have been' stacks inversion + modal perfect and momentarily reads as scrambled, but the 'just as ..., so + aux + S' rule resolves it cleanly. (E) briefly invites a singular/plural double-take that dissolves on locating the head noun 'analyses'. (B) is unambiguously wrong under the with-absolute rule and no alternative parse (reduced relative, new finite clause, ellipsis) rescues it. Single defensible answer: (B).
